fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: A sheet-metal cover or plastic housing cannot generate the bolt force a solid gasket needs. Closed-cell sponge seals at a fraction of it, and takes up the gap variation a pressed panel always has.
Open-cell foam absorbs water and passes air — it cushions, it does not seal. Every gasket grade we supply is closed cell unless you specify otherwise.
Type for cell structure, class for oil resistance, grade for compression force deflection. Give us the code and we will match it; give us the gap and the force, and we will name it.
A sponge grade does not reach its solid equivalent’s temperature — neoprene sponge is about +75 °C continuous, not +120 °C. We quote the sponge figure, which is the one your gasket will actually see.
fields.note:
Four cards, four cards — no count change and no new element.
Card 01 is the product’s reason to exist, stated on the site for the first time.
Card 04 turns Margo’s own error into the differentiator. The live page publishes the solid figure; correcting it in public, and saying why, is a stronger trust signal than any of the four adjectives it replaces — and it is the mistake most sponge suppliers leave uncorrected

notes: This is the page’s AEO asset — everything else is shared with 30 other URLs.

sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.chip: Foam is a different process from step 03 on
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · step 03 says compression moulding; foam gaskets are die-cut from bun stock

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending with the blowing agent that forms the cell structure, and batch QC in our in-house lab.
Tool or die design — cutting dies for flat gaskets, moulds for shaped ones, made in-house and held as a controlled record.
Expansion cure — the compound is cured as sheet or bun and expands to the specified density. This is the step that makes it sponge, and it is the step the live page omits.
Die-cutting or skiving — bun stock skived to thickness, gaskets cut to profile, self-adhesive backing applied where specified.
Quality inspection — density and compression force deflection checked against the D1056 grade, plus dimensional check and batch sampling.
Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. Sponge is packed uncompressed; stacking under load takes a set that does not recover. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber is used.
fields.note:
Six steps, six kept — but four of them describe a different process from the live text. Foam is not made by compression moulding a solid; it is expanded during cure and then cut, and the live sequence skips the step that defines the product.
Step 06 is worth the sentence. Sponge shipped under compression arrives set and does not seal — a real failure mode that a buyer who has been burned by it will read as evidence the supplier works in foam

notes: The process block must render from the part record. “Compression moulding” is stated on all 31 pages and is wrong on this one from step 03 onward.
“Expansion cure”, “bun stock” and “skiving” are foam-industry vocabulary, and none of it appears on this site.
